mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may indicate broader economic slowdown and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE rises above 4%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in both GDP and housing starts indicates weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 12-month averages, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production during a late-cycle expansion signals supply chain constraints or reduced production, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when INDPRO is declining during a late-cycle expansion, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth indicates a robust labor market, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month average, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in real federal spending indicates increased demand, which stimulates economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when RSAFS is more than 5% above its 6-month average, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is strong but inflation is high, the combination may lead to stagflation, which reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when GDPC1 is strong but CPIAUCSL is high, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in 3 months, this hypothesis is rejected.
